why: A = exists_scPlusSection_linAt ∧ lemma_5_3_17 (universes 0). B is Lemma 5.24 in the setting of Lemma 5.23: tame strong bundle, AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak, f with tame germ data (germ reading), x a smooth zero, Z a smooth line splitting T_zO = Z ⊕ ker dt(x), b : T_xS → Z with dt∘b = τ, and any open V ∋ x. A ⇒ B fails only at the bump-function hypothesis. B gives a bump f ≢ 0, while A needs f(x) ≠ 0 (the construction uses β = 1 near x, Proposition 5.30), and the project has only strong ⇒ weak. With the strong reading it is proved: A_to_BStrong (#rt_check OK). It writes b v = (τ v/dt(x)ζ)·ζ and puts Dg(ζ) in K_{φ(x)} via rho_scDeriv_comp_r at the zero. Dg(ζ) is smooth by the level operators, so it is Φ(e)₂ for a smooth e over x. A Hahn–Banach extension ℓ of −τ/dt(x)ζ then feeds A's exists_scPlusSection_linAt; no finite-dimensionality of T_xS is needed. B ⇒ A fails genuinely. A prescribes s'(x) on all of T_zO for an arbitrary functional ℓ and smooth e, and allows an arbitrary section f and finite-dimensional K, with no tame strong bundle and no t or Z. B only controls s'(x) on ker f'(x) for b into a smooth complement of ker dt(x), under extra tameness hypotheses.
B_issue: Not a bug, but the same reading choice as V5_29/V5_38/V5_39/V5_45, and it decides A ⇒ B: 'bump functions' is read as AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak (f not identically zero), whereas the project uses f(x) ≠ 0. The blind author flags this caveat. B also adds IsTameStrongBundle, which is not needed (A_to_BStrong ignores it).
intended: BStrong (B with AdmitsBumpFunctions) is implied by A (A_to_BStrong) and by B (BStrong_of_B), so the bump-function reading is the only obstruction to A ⇒ B.
